result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You came to hospital after a fall at home. You hit your head. You did not lose consciousness.

- Your right hip X-ray shows no fracture (broken bone).
- Your head scan (CT) shows no bleeding inside the head.
- Your blood pressure was 142/80 lying down. It was 108/66 standing up.
- This is called postural hypotension. It means your blood pressure drops when you stand up.
- Your medicine amlodipine may be causing this drop. This is possible, not certain.

## What you need to do
1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 mg.
2. Do not stop your other medicines. Keep taking them.
3. Stand up slowly.
4. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
5. Watch for a letter from the Falls Prevention Clinic. It will give you an appointment.
6. Your GP will check your blood pressure again in 4 weeks. They will check it lying and standing.

## Dates and medicines
- 14 October 2026: the date you were seen at hospital.
- In 4 weeks: your GP rechecks your blood pressure, lying and standing.
- Falls Prevention Clinic: no appointment date is given yet.
- Amlodipine 10 mg: STOP. It may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
- All other medicines: no change. Keep taking them.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will my Falls Prevention Clinic appointment be?
- Why might amlodipine be making my blood pressure drop when I stand?
- What can I do to stand up more safely?

## When to get urgent help
In the next few days, you might get a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness. If so, call 999 or go to A&E.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
